verdict.rationale: Galileo's logging docs say it captures every session, trace, and span once instrumented. Spans sharing a trace ID are joined into a single trace, including across agents in different processes, and the Python SDK's @log decorator logs spans. Multi-agent LangGraph tutorials surface session-level metrics, so the core of the story is first-party documented. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of parent/child span nesting within a trace, detail on thread-style grouping beyond sessions, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trace multi-step agent runs as nested spans grouped into sessions or threads

citations.quote: Once instrumented, Galileo captures every session, trace, and span, producing a structured stream of real-time data.
Galileo joins all spans that share a trace ID into a single trace.
Stitch traces across two agents in different processes using OTel and the GalileoSpanProcessor.
You can also use the `@log` decorator to log spans.
Add Galileo evaluations to a multi-agent LangGraph app, View and understand session level metrics
